messages:
alex: Hey team — our CI started failing on every deploy to staging with 401s against the Redwood API about 2 hours after we tightened the service account token TTL to 10m. Deploys used to pass. deploy-bot: pipeline #342 failed stage=deploy status=401 :disappointed:

morgan: @alex can you paste the exact response body/header you see? is it an expired token or permission denied?

alex: here's the curl we run from the runner and the response: 
```
$ curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer $CI_SA_TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/models
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 04 Feb 2025 15:12:03 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 92
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error=\"invalid_token\", error_description=\"token expired\"
{"error":"invalid_token","message":"token expired"}
```
This token was created ~9m30s before the request (we log creation time). So it's not fully expired but close.

jess: :eyes: that smells like a propagation/clock-skew + refresh window issue. Two quick Qs: what creates the token (GitLab runner OIDC or CI service account short-lived key) and are runners using a local cache?

alex: GitLab CI obtains an ephemeral SA token via our token-exchange service (we call /internal/sa/exchange which returns a JWT with a 10m ttl). Runners reuse the token across multiple pods if the job matrix forks quickly. We saw it fail more when matrix parallelism is high.

morgan: ok that matches a race: token TTL=10m, job startup + network jitter + proxy + k8s image pull can push first request close to expiry. If token refresh happens only after failure, many parallel jobs will all try the same exchange and some get a slightly older token.

liam: can you confirm runner clock skew? also what is the token issuance time in the JWT (iat/exp)? paste decoded header (mask sensitive fields).

alex: decoded exp/iat snippet: 
```
{ "iat": 1707064200, "exp": 1707064800 }
```
so 600s exactly. Runner host clocks look fine within <2s.

jess: two-pronged mitigation: 1) add a refresh-buffer on the client (fail if token age > TTL - 30s, proactively fetch new token); 2) increase short-lived token TTL to 15m while we patch runner behavior. Prefer (1) for least-privilege/security but (2) buys time.

morgan: also check that token-exchange service returns a fresh token per request (no stale cache). if you cache by SA id+job id you could hand out near-expiry tokens under load.

alex: confirmed token-exchange was returning cached tokens for identical job args for 30s window — we added caching to reduce backend calls. That explains why many jobs got the same near-expiry token. :facepalm:

liam: nice find. short-term: disable caching or reduce to 5s; long-term: client-side refresh buffer + jitter when getting tokens so you don't thundering-herd the exchange endpoint.

jess: add this repro/test to support docs: minimal script to reproduce under parallel runners. e.g.: 
```
# spawn N parallel requests that all request a token and then immediately call API
for i in $(seq 1 20); do (
  TOKEN=$(curl -sS https://internal/token-exchange -d '{"job":1}')
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/status &
) & done; wait
```
This will surface stale/cached tokens returning 401s when TTL is tight.

morgan: recommendations summary I put in the ticket: 
- Disable caching on token-exchange or shrink cache TTL -> 0-5s.
- Implement client refresh buffer (reject tokens older than TTL-30s) and jittered refresh to avoid thundering herd.
- Consider increasing issuance TTL to 15m for high-parallelism pipelines as temporary mitigation.
- Audit runner and token-exchange clocks and network path for added latency.
- Confirm role bindings are least-privilege (we noticed the token-exchange currently grants broad 'inference.admin' during exchange; recommend issuing scoped tokens with narrow perms required for deploy).

alex: I'm going to push a small change to token-exchange cache to 3s and add client-side buffer logic in the runner image. Will report back after a few runs. Thanks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: pipeline #343 triggered (staging) by alex — running with cache=3s.

morgan: great — please ping if it still fails. If the fixes hold, we'll make the client refresh buffer standard in our CI templates and add an example in the docs for 'CI service account best practices'.

liam: also opened a follow-up to evaluate switching to OIDC tokens per-job (no caching) for runners that support it — lower blast radius and aligns with least-privilege.

alex: update: after reducing cache and adding buffer the last 5 matrix runs passed. marking as resolved for now, will close ticket after 24h of stability.

morgan: resolved -> monitoring. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
